introduction: “If, during the seed-sowing time, we want to gather the harvest, we shall fail.” The passages gathered here insist that in this period teaching the Faith comes before every other activity, including good ones; ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says it of assemblies, conventions and charitable work, and Shoghi Effendi explains that the turmoil of the age makes the claim more urgent, since the Bahá’ís believe they hold the remedy. The Gospels have the same hard priority in several sayings: “one thing is needful”, “let the dead bury their dead”, “seek ye first the kingdom”, and the apostles’ refusal to “leave the word of God, and serve tables”. James’s rebuke of faith that says “be ye warmed and filled” and does nothing is the necessary check.
questions: What is the argument for putting teaching before relief of immediate need? What would have to be true for it to hold?
The apostles appointed others to serve tables; they did not stop the tables. What does that suggest about how a priority is kept?
How would you answer someone who found reading 4 hard-hearted?

outside.why: Seed-time is for sowing. To every thing there is a season: a time to plant, and a time to pluck up that which is planted.
Say not ye, there are yet four months; lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest.
An Assembly occupied with anything else spends its time in futility. The Twelve: it is not reason that we should leave the word of God, and serve tables.
The greatest of all matters today. Necessity is laid upon me; yea, woe is unto me, if I preach not the gospel.
Ministering to the weak is good, yet for two hundred years all thought must be for teaching. Ye have the poor with you always, and whensoever ye will ye may do them good: but me ye have not always.

James would not let such a priority stand unqualified: if a brother or sister be naked, and destitute of daily food, and one say, be ye warmed and filled, what doth it profit? How does reading 10 keep the priority from becoming indifference?
Nothing else will benefit. Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things: but one thing is needful.
This is the day of teaching. I must work while it is day: the night cometh, when no man can work.
Now is the time for foundations, not decoration. Let the dead bury their dead: but go thou and preach the kingdom of God.
Not to sit idle while the world’s problems grow. Seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
The opportunities which the turmoil of the age presents. Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
